rows.text: The Gemma B70 decode benchmark evaluates autoregressive throughput under varying sequence lengths. To establish a valid benchmark, the hardware must maintain high memory bandwidth to prevent the benchmark from becoming compute-bound. During the decode benchmark, the primary bottleneck is the KV cache retrieval speed, which dictates the benchmark results. A consistent benchmark requires fixed batch sizes to ensure the benchmark measures pure decoding latency rather than scheduling overhead. In this benchmark, token-per-second metrics serve as the primary benchmark indicator. If the benchmark shows high variance, the benchmark environment must be re-calibrated. Ultimately, the Gemma B70 decode benchmark provides a standardized benchmark for comparing inference efficiency across different GPU architectures.
